title: Rafael and the Verdict
premise: When the coffin of Ashgrove's founder, Edmund Verity, is found empty during a ceremonial exhumation, true-crime podcaster Vesper Thornbury realizes the town that raised her has been protecting a twelve-year-old disappearance disguised as a death. Her investigation collides with her loyalty to Rafael Okafor, the sheriff who once saved her from becoming a story himself, and whose family name appears in a ledger hidden in the founder's memorial clock. As the trial of the accused gravedigger approaches, Vesper must choose between publishing the truth that will destroy Rafael's standing and burying it forever. She broadcasts the full ledger, clearing Rafael's father but implicating the town council, and finally claims her place in Ashgrove not as its invisible archivist but as its conscience.
about_author: Noor Halloran is a former court stenographer from coastal Maine who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries about communities that mistake silence for peace.

chapters.title: The Empty Suit
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. At the bicentennial exhumation, the coffin holding founder Edmund Verity opens to reveal nothing but river stones and a child's shoe. Vesper, who has spent twelve years filing the town's secrets instead of reporting them, recognizes the shoe as belonging to a boy who vanished in 2013. The chapter ends with her deciding, trembling, to open a case file she swore she'd never start. Emotional beat: dread cracking into resolve.

chapters.title: Ledger of Hours
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV, with an intercut of Rafael's. Sheriff Rafael Okafor warns her off, revealing the accused gravedigger is his own cousin, and the trial begins in three weeks. Vesper discovers the founder's memorial clock face is a coded ledger: dates, initials, payments. One entry names Rafael's father as recipient of hush money the year the boy disappeared. Emotional beat: intimacy curdling into suspicion as love and duty pull opposite directions.

chapters.title: What the Clock Kept
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Decoding the final cipher at night in the records office, she learns the council paid Rafael's father to stay silent after he found the boy's body, and that the 'founder' faked his own death decades ago, his coffin a rotating hiding place. Rafael catches her there; they confront each other, and he admits he suspected but chose the town over truth. Climactic beat: betrayal confessed, and Vesper choosing to publish anyway, alone.

chapters.title: Verdict
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, converging on the courthouse steps. Vesper airs the decoded ledger hours before the verdict, exonerating the cousin and indicting five council members, including the mayor who once protected her. Rafael publicly corroborates her evidence, sacrificing his badge to stand beside her. The empty coffin is reburied with the boy's name spoken aloud. Final beat: belonging earned through truth, and the two walking home together through a town that finally sees them.
